title: Practice: Arc Length and Sector Area

questions.stem: A sector has radius 12 cm and angle 150 degrees. What is the arc length in terms of pi?
questions.explanation: Arc length = (theta/360) x 2 pi r = (150/360) x 2 pi x 12 = (5/12) x 24 pi = 10 pi cm.

questions.stem: A sector has radius 8 cm and angle 90 degrees. What is the area of the sector in terms of pi?
questions.explanation: Sector area = (theta/360) x pi r^2 = (90/360) x pi x 64 = (1/4) x 64 pi = 16 pi cm squared.

questions.stem: A sector has an arc length of 6 pi cm and a radius of 9 cm. What is the angle of the sector?
questions.explanation: Arc length = (theta/360) x 2 pi r. So 6 pi = (theta/360) x 18 pi. Dividing both sides by pi: 6 = (theta/360) x 18. So theta/360 = 6/18 = 1/3. Therefore theta = 120 degrees.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of a sector with radius 10 cm and angle 72 degrees? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: Perimeter = arc length + 2 radii. Arc length = (72/360) x 2 pi x 10 = (1/5) x 20 pi = 4 pi = 12.566... cm. Perimeter = 12.566 + 10 + 10 = 32.6 cm (1 d.p.).

questions.stem: A sector has radius 6 cm and area 15 pi cm squared. What is the angle of the sector?
questions.explanation: Area = (theta/360) x pi r^2. So 15 pi = (theta/360) x 36 pi. Dividing by pi: 15 = (theta/360) x 36. So theta/360 = 15/36 = 5/12. Therefore theta = 5/12 x 360 = 150 degrees.
